description: Adversarial semantic retrieval benchmark; original lexical baseline remains separate.

documents.title: Annual leave entitlement
documents.text: After the accrual period is completed, employees receive thirty consecutive calendar days of annual leave for rest and recovery.

documents.title: Business-day leave policy
documents.text: After the accrual period, employees receive twenty business days of leave; weekends and public holidays are excluded.

documents.title: Mutual TLS authentication
documents.text: Mutual TLS, abbreviated mTLS, authenticates both endpoints by requiring certificates from the client and the server during the handshake.

documents.title: Server TLS authentication
documents.text: Server-side TLS encrypts traffic and authenticates the server, while the client connects without presenting a certificate.

documents.title: Tail latency percentile
documents.text: P95 latency is the response-time threshold that at least ninety-five percent of requests meet or beat; it exposes slow-tail behavior.

documents.title: Average latency
documents.text: Mean latency is the arithmetic average of request durations and can hide a small group of extremely slow requests.

documents.title: SQLite write-ahead logging
documents.text: SQLite write-ahead logging, or WAL mode, lets readers continue while a writer appends changes to a log; checkpointing later merges those changes.

documents.title: SQLite rollback journal
documents.text: SQLite rollback-journal mode records original pages before replacing the database and commonly serializes readers with a writer.

documents.title: MCP per-tool authorization
documents.text: An MCP scope such as tools:calculator grants permission to invoke one named tool; broad roles do not replace per-tool authorization.

documents.title: MCP role authorization
documents.text: A role groups several permissions for a principal, but a role alone does not prove that a specific MCP tool scope was granted.

documents.title: Grounded retrieval abstention
documents.text: A grounded RAG assistant should abstain when retrieved context does not contain evidence for the requested claim instead of inventing an answer.

documents.title: Ungrounded answer risk
documents.text: A hallucinated answer presents unsupported claims as facts even when the retrieval context is empty or irrelevant.

documents.title: Safe retry policy
documents.text: Automatic retries are safest for idempotent operations; retrying a non-idempotent write can duplicate its side effect.

documents.title: Retry backoff
documents.text: Exponential backoff spaces repeated attempts so a failing dependency is not overwhelmed by synchronized clients.

documents.title: Continuous integration gates
documents.text: A CI pipeline should run tests, type checks, security audits and packaging gates before a change is promoted.

documents.title: Continuous deployment
documents.text: A deployment workflow publishes an already validated artifact to a runtime environment and can trigger a rollback.

documents.title: Distributed trace identity
documents.text: A distributed trace links request, router, retrieval and tool spans through one shared trace identifier.

documents.title: Metrics versus traces
documents.text: A metric aggregates measurements over time, while a trace preserves the causal sequence of spans for one request.

documents.title: Tool timeout boundary
documents.text: A tool timeout bounds how long the host waits for a tool; cancelling the caller does not forcibly kill an already running Python thread.

documents.title: Tool retry behavior
documents.text: A retry policy decides whether a failed tool call may be attempted again and should consider idempotency before repeating it.

documents.title: RBAC and tenant isolation
documents.text: Role-based access control grants permissions through roles, while tenant isolation prevents a principal from reading another tenant's resources.

documents.title: Document ACL
documents.text: A document ACL lists the principals allowed to read one document and is narrower than a role shared across a tenant.

documents.title: Recovery point objective
documents.text: RPO is the maximum acceptable amount of data loss expressed as elapsed time between the latest recoverable copy and an incident.

documents.title: Recovery time objective
documents.text: RTO is the target time to restore a service after disruption, not the amount of data that may be lost.
